hook: Why your seedlings get tall and floppy

slides.t: Late winter sun is weak and short. Seedlings stretch toward it and grow thin, pale stems.
A full spectrum light gives seedlings strong, even light from above, so they grow short and sturdy.
Hang the light just a few inches above the leaves and raise it as they grow. Follow the maker's distance guide.
Most seedlings do well with 14 to 16 hours of light a day. They still need a few hours of dark to rest.
Indoor plants need a week or so of short outdoor visits before planting out, or the sun and wind can shock them.

hook: A gift for the gardener who has everything
hook_sub: A tin full of next year's garden

slides.t: A sealed pack of many vegetable varieties, sized to plant a whole garden and keep some in reserve.
Heirloom, open-pollinated seeds grow true to type, so a gardener can save seed from the best plants each year.
Seeds last longest cool, dark and dry. A closet shelf beats a hot garage or a damp shed.
Roll 10 seeds in a damp paper towel. After a week, count how many sprouted to see how well they'll grow.
It gives a gardener something to sort and dream over all winter, long before the soil warms up.
